---
title: "Deciles and quartiles of posterior means"
subtitle: "3.9 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figures 2C and 6"
description: "Evaluation of fixed posterior-mean tiers on KRW's discordance and informativeness axes."
---

Quartiles and deciles split firms into nearly equal groups by posterior mean, keeping exact score ties together.
We compare these reports with archived cards using Kline, Rose and Walters's measures of discordance and
informativeness. Both calculations use the released pair probabilities. In each example below, the selected
archived card makes fewer expected wrong directions per possible pair and provides more information than the
fixed tiers. The comparison evaluates reports that have already been chosen.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race quartiles, card λ .60.** The quartile point has DR .1696 and I .4185. The ringed card has lower DR,
  .1678, and higher I, .4336. The size patterns show how the card's grade boundaries differ from the nearly equal quartiles.
- **Race deciles, card λ .82.** Deciles move to DR .2271 and I .4550, while the selected card reaches .2243
  and .4589. The deciles disclose more pairs than the quartiles. The selected card still has lower DR and higher I.
- **Gender quartiles, card λ .64.** Under the signed male-name contact-gap target, quartiles have DR .1978
  and I .3621; the card gives .1908 and .3875. These coordinates concern a different target from the race comparisons.
- **Gender deciles, card λ .80.** Deciles give DR .2525 and I .4042; the card gives .2373 and .4078.
  The comparison depends on the selected λ. The selected card need not improve both coordinates at every grid setting.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
KRW discuss deciles and quartiles in §IV.B and Figure 2C, and reporting possibilities in §V.E and Figure 6.
The diamonds show the fixed tiers. The curve joins cards that KRW selected using their archived probabilities.
We recompute each card's coordinates with the released probabilities without rerunning that search. KRW use τ̄
for informativeness. For gender, the target is the signed contact gap.

Data: Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700; deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1, CC-BY-NC,

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
x <- postrank::pr_case_krw$alternatives$race
b <- postrank::postrank_cuts(setNames(x$summaries$means[,1],x$entity_ids),x,postrank::postrank_settings(weights=c(race_signed=1),tau=.375,G_max=10),direction="descending",rule="quantile",G_b=4,method="posterior_mean")
b$evaluation[c("N","E_over_N","primary_risk")]
```
:::

Standalone: [deciles-quartiles](../../embed/deciles-quartiles.html), for example `?criterion=race&G=4&lambda=.60`.

Related applications: [Tiers and optimized cuts of posterior rankings](posterior-tiers.qmd), [Fixed quantile tiers](fixed-tiers.qmd).
